english.notes:
(i) Consider section 1(1) of the Malicious Communications Act 1988 which covers offences in relation to sending of indecent, offensive or threatening letters, electronic communications or articles with intent to cause the recipient distress or anxiety.
(ii) Consider also an offence under the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.
(iii) See also offences wordings H5556, H5557, H5558 and H5559.
(iv) As of 13th April 2015, the time limit on prosecution for offences under section 127 of the Communications Act 2003 has been amended. An information or complaint must be laid before the end of the period of 3 years beginning with the day on which the offence was committed, and before the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the day on which evidence comes to the knowledge of the prosecutor which the prosecutor considers sufficient to justify proceedings.
(v) The amendment to the time limit (outlined in note (iv) above) applies only in relation to an offence committed on or after 13th April 2015 - for offences committed prior to this date the time limit on prosecution is 6 months from the date of commission of the offence.
(vi) Please see CPS guidelines on Prosecuting Cases Involving Communications Sent via Social Media as an approval from the Director’s Legal Advisor may be applicable.

Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
